method_note: As with the arithmetic file: distribution-only descriptions, ground-truth label withheld, candidate constructs listed in the prompt. SUPERSEDED FOR NUMBERS: the underlying codenet_v9 R1 rows were computed at batch 32 and are contaminated by the left-padding alignment bug (prefill chunk k maps to source chunk k only when pad_len % L == 0). The interpreter's *behaviour* below is still informative — in particular its refusal to invent patterns for near-chance codes — but the per-code lifts it was shown are not the clean values. See codenet_gate.md for batch-1 numbers.

results.description: Fires only at chunk d0 (the very first chunk of every file) with 3.8x lift toward one construct category, marking the file's opening chunk - plausibly an import or top-level module statement.
results.note: Position call correct, construct call wrong (guessed import, actual FunctionDef). WITHDRAWN ANYWAY: clean measurement gives lift_pos = 1.00x - this code is P(FunctionDef | chunk 0), a fact about Python file structure, not a learned detector.

results.description: A rare code (n=38) that is unusually concentrated on one specific construct category (45% purity, 3.3x lift) and recurs at many different chunk positions (18 of 32) rather than being tied to one file location, suggesting it tracks a specific construct type wherever it occurs in the file.
results.note: Correct shape (distributed construct tracker, not positional). Clean batch-1 measurement weakens it to lift_pos 1.68x, p_bonf = 1 - does not survive correction.

results.description: Spread across almost every chunk position in the file (31 of 32) with only a modest skew (1.9x lift) toward a category rarer than call expressions, giving a weak but non-trivial construct association rather than a clean pattern.
results.note: Holds up under batch-1: If, lift_pos 1.73x across 31 positions.

results.description: Purity and lift are essentially at the corpus base rate for call expressions (1.1x lift) - no clear pattern beyond reflecting the dominant background construct frequency.
results.note: Correctly called at chance. Under batch-1 this code is actually t8 -> Return, lift_pos 5.41x, p_bonf 6e-11 - the padding bug had hidden a real detector behind a chance-level Call assignment.

results.description: Like t8, its top category purity matches the call-expression base rate almost exactly (1.1x lift) - no clear discriminative pattern.

The largest python code (n=1275), spread over nearly all positions, with purity essentially equal to the call-expression base rate (1.06x lift) - no clear pattern, functions as a generic/default code.

summary.negative_control: All three codes at ~1.1x lift were labelled 'no clear pattern'. The interpreter did not manufacture findings where the statistics did not support them.
summary.caveat: One consequence of the padding bug is visible here: code 8 was shown as a chance-level Call code and correctly called as such, but the clean measurement reveals it as the study's strongest CodeNet detector (Return, lift_pos 5.41x). The interpreter was right about the data it was given; the data was wrong.
